[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;59688961]Late in the night, a young man is walking home in the city of Aduab. Sitting down on a streetcorner, he opens his bottle of soda and takes a sip. Even though he should go home, he feels something big will happen, and he's right. Looking up, a full moon helps illuminate a small plane looking thing in the sky as it flies overhead and then out of sight overhead the buildings around him. He wonders for a second what it could have possibly been, and then a blast booms through the night silence, answering his question. He stands in shock for a few seconds before another blast goes off, bringing him back to reality. Thinking quickly, he rushes to the closest building with a basement he knows of which is his local hospital. Arriving, the staff enlist him and whoever they can into helping them move patients to the basement throughout the night. As the sun comes up the next morning, the blasts have stopped and the hospital is fine. Checking social media, he sees an address from Lavia is being posted all over. Wondering what this is, he clicks and turns his volume up just enough to hear it.

Two days ago, militants kidnapped eight people on a private trip. Last night, we, in retaliation, deployed 80 glidebombs from airbases in Kalnaka. We hit only strategic and governmental targets in the city of Aduab and surrounding towns. A screen behind the man changes from the Lavian seal to a satellite image of a burning refinery. By hitting this refinery and others like it, we cripple the little industry Sal-Baliz still has and cost them much more than any ransom would cost us. The image switches again, this time to a port. We arent foolish, we know where their fleet is, so we make an offer to the board at SummitOne. We know all you care about is money, as every company does, and ports are a very important part of your supply train, so would you rather expel these terrorist forces from your port, or have them sunk in it and have to spend tens of thousands removing their flaming hulls. And to the terrorists of Sal-Baliz, I know you hate us, but Im not sure youre stupid, so I'll offer this just in case. You can release the hostages like civil people, or we can keep launching cheap munitions into your remaining industry. Honestly, Id take freeing eight people over a complete halt to any manufacturing my country has. Hard to be on holy war when youd struggle to scrounge up enough bullets from your cratered factories.

The screen returns to the seal, and the man pauses for a little, thinking. We care for our fellow citizens, and the death of them would mean proportional destruction of the Sal-Baliz territory. Then after that, the recording ends.[/quote]

Just hours after the attack, the Sal-Baliz would issue a short online statement to the government of Lavia.

[i]4 of the 8 hostages will be returned. Expect a vessel to arrive at your most northern port within 48 hours. Do not fire upon this ship or all of the hostages will be killed and the Al-Qadi will be unleashed. The remaining 4 hostages will be kept in custody until you provide us with funds and materials originally requested. Failure to comply within 48 hours will result in the death of the remaining hostages.[/i]

[b][i]THE EEHP NEGOTIATIONS FINISH! (FINALY)[/i][/b]

The Erene Economic and Humanitarian Pact and it's members have decided on the first iteration of it's carter!

1. Travel and Immigration:
	1A: The members of the EEHP will allow for visa-free travel between each member, bringing the benefit of increased tourism and a larger sense of collaboration. Visa-free travel is available for those who are visiting or simply traveling through a member country. 

1B: Each member is allowed to manage their own immigration laws and work visa requirements, although these requirements shall follow the human right policies of the EEHP. If a member does not follow the human rights requirements, a consul of other members will decide a time limit for the nation to fix their mistake, or they will be kicked out of the EEHP.

	1B2: If an immigrant is denied entry to the nation they are applying to and they do not have the capabilities or finances to travel back home, they will be supplied with a bus ticket to facilitate their travel to a nearby airport and airline ticket to either their home country or country they have citizenship to.

2. Trade, Technology sharing, and Business laws inside the EEHP:

2A: Members of the EEHP will share the same level of safety standards and regulations allowing for standardized punishments and more streamlined certificate applications by allowing a business to use one certificate in all EEHP countries. This will allow for the encouragement of EEHP regulations and safety standards as well as increased trade between EEHP members

	2A1: As some practices have been around for hundreds of years, the EEHP will allow specific historical trades to be issued a special EEHP safety exception letter. However, these workplaces will still be required to provide any needed safety equipment and tools to ensure worker health (ie masks, gloves, boots, ect.)

2B: All EEHP members shall enact a small 1% tariff on all other EEHP members. This is to enable small businesses and local brands to compete with outside companies as 2A makes it easier for companies to expand to other member states. 

2C: All members shall implement EEHP safety and workplace guidelines or have a chance to have their license revoked. These guidelines include but are not limited to absolutely no discrimination (race, skin color, religion (exceptions made for religious institutions such as churches or mosques), gender, or sexual identity), implementation of minimum wage (decided by the member state), training and educating employees on best waste disposal practices for their workplace, and practice of best workplace safety guidelines decided on by the EEHP.

	2C1: All companies will be liable to lawsuits and fines for not following EEHP guidelines, however companies will specifically be required to properly dispose of their waste under EEHP regulations or be fined an amount of 1% of their yearly income for the first offence. A second offence calls for a 5% fine of the yearly income, and a third offence comes with a 10% fine of the yearly income than the removal of the companys EEHP business operating licenses.  

2D: EEHP members will agree to share all knowledge and technology that have been proven to positively impact overall quality of life. This includes medical breakthroughs, medicine patents, power generation, recycling, waste disposal, transport, and certain digital technologies. Companies that produce these and have their invention/technology shared will get a yearly sum of money as compensation, which will be decided by EEHP analysts. 

3. Trade and Business outside the EEHP:
3A: Members will impose tariffs and import restrictions upon nations that violate human rights guidelines set by the EEHP. This will also include nations considered dictatorships by the EEHP, or monarchies that dont practice the minimum requirements for democratic involvement of the people. 

		3A1: Companies that violate EEHP human rights guidelines shall also be sanctioned if they use such means, however if their home country has these violations outlawed and the company is outsourcing its work to a country that does violate guidelines, then solely the company will be tariffed.
